---
title: "SLA PSO Time-to-Done Breach Rate"
description: "Share of PSOM tickets that missed the PSO time-to-done SLA."
---

The proportion of PSOM tickets that missed the "Time to Done - PSO" SLA, based
on the latest snapshot.

This metric reflects how well the PSO team is resolving tickets within the
agreed timeframe, counting only the time the ticket is with that team. Unlike
the whole-ticket [SLA Time-to-Done Breach Rate](sla-time-to-done-breach-rate.qmd),
its clock pauses while the ticket is escalated. Like that SLA, it also pauses
while waiting for the customer. Only tickets where the SLA clock started are
included; tickets with no clock are excluded.

## Calculation

From [`jira.psom_sla`](../../catalog/jira/psom_sla.qmd), filter
to the most recent `date` partition, to `sla = 'pso_time_to_done'`, and to rows
where `breached` is not null (i.e., the clock started). Divide the count of
rows where `breached` is true by the total count of those rows.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_sla_tickets,
    SUM(CASE WHEN breached THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS breached_count,
    CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN breached THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE)
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS breach_rate
FROM jira.psom_sla
WHERE date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM jira.psom_sla)
  AND sla = 'pso_time_to_done'
  AND breached IS NOT NULL;
```

## R

```r
psom_sla <- tbl(con, in_schema("jira", "psom_sla"))
latest_date <- psom_sla |> summarise(d = max(date, na.rm = TRUE)) |> pull(d)

psom_sla |>
  filter(
    as.Date(date) == as.Date(latest_date),
    sla == "pso_time_to_done",
    !is.na(breached)
  ) |>
  summarise(
    total_sla_tickets = n(),
    breached_count    = sum(as.integer(breached), na.rm = TRUE),
    breach_rate       = sum(as.integer(breached), na.rm = TRUE) / as.double(n())
  )
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

The rate is a proportion between 0 and 1. Tickets whose
clock never started (null `breached`) are excluded from both numerator and
denominator. Check `total_sla_tickets` to understand the sample size underlying
the rate.

This clock only started on tickets created from about 2026-08-06, and the
older snapshots have no `pso_time_to_done` rows, so the sample is smaller than
for the other SLAs. The goal is set per ticket and counted in working hours
(09:00 to 17:00), so a breach means the ticket missed its own target.

A ticket that is still open and inside its goal is recorded as not breached
(`false`), the same as a ticket that met the SLA. The rate on a live snapshot
is therefore a lower bound: some of those open tickets may still breach before
they are resolved. It is most meaningful once the snapshot's tickets are
largely resolved.

## Alternative names

- PSO touchtime SLA breach rate
- PSO time to done SLA compliance
- PSO time-to-done SLA failure rate
